lines.trans: There goes Judge Mateo with the first bite: nobody say a single word!
Look how smoothly the fork glides to the bottom without a hammer or workshop glasses.
Wait... let a man chew in peace before you start celebrating.
He took a second bite! Rocio, he did not make the brass-polishing face!
Well, Mateo? Tell us the truth: does it deserve to be on our Saturday anniversary table?
Hand me my paper notebook and my carpenter pencil from beside the teapot, Clara.
He is writing in big letters... TEN OUT OF TEN, DO NOT CHANGE A THING!
YES! A ten out of ten in Mateo's pencil is worth three gold medals!
Purely for technical safety, mind you, I should test one more small corner slice.

words.gloss: corner (outer street corner or cake corner)

lines.trans: Aha! We caught you asking for another slice, Mr Strict Judge!
Eat all you want, Mateo, and write down four whole cakes for Saturday!
Keep baking like this, Rocio, and half of Valencia will line up outside our gate.

lines.trans: Aha! We caught you asking for another slice, Mr Strict Judge!
Eat all you want, Mateo, and write down four whole cakes for Saturday!
Keep baking like this, Rocio, and half of Valencia will line up outside our gate.
See you!

meanings.note: Marks destination, clock time, and animate direct objects (personal a).

examples.text: Vamos a la estación ahora.
examples.trans: We are going to the station now.

examples.text: El desayuno empieza a las ocho.
examples.trans: Breakfast starts at eight o'clock.

meanings.note: Exclamation of discovery or agreement.

examples.text: ¡Ajá, aquí estaban mis gafas!
examples.trans: Aha, here were my glasses!

examples.text: Ajá, eso explica el ruido.
examples.trans: Aha, that explains the noise.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition a + masculine article el; al + infinitive means 'upon doing'.

examples.text: Vamos al mercado por la mañana.
examples.trans: We go to the market in the morning.

examples.text: Al abrir la puerta, sonó el timbre.
examples.trans: Upon opening the door, the bell rang.

meanings.note: Allá va is a natural everyday phrase before flipping a switch or starting something.

examples.text: Allá va la primera prueba de la lámpara.
examples.trans: Here goes the first test of the lamp.

examples.text: Pon las sillas plegadas más allá del arco.
examples.trans: Put the folded chairs further past the arch.

meanings.note: Used for yearly celebrations of weddings, foundations, or historic dates.

examples.text: El próximo sábado celebramos el trigésimo aniversario en la posada.
examples.trans: Next Saturday we celebrate the thirtieth anniversary at the inn.

examples.text: Prepararon un pastel especial para el aniversario del barrio.
examples.trans: They baked a special cake for the neighbourhood anniversary.

meanings.note: Antes de means 'before' a noun or infinitive.

examples.text: Llegué diez minutos antes.
examples.trans: I arrived ten minutes early.

examples.text: Antes de salir, cierra la ventana.
examples.trans: Before leaving, close the window.

meanings.note: Everyday word in Spain for writing down a note or phone number.

examples.text: Apunto la dirección en un papel.
examples.trans: I jot down the address on a piece of paper.

examples.text: ¿Apuntaste el nombre del cliente?
examples.trans: Did you write down the guest's name?

meanings.note: Así que means 'so / therefore'.

examples.text: Hazlo así, despacio.
examples.trans: Do it like this, slowly.

examples.text: Llueve mucho, así que entramos.
examples.trans: It is raining hard, so let us go inside.

meanings.note: Before an adjective (bien caliente), means 'nice and hot'.

examples.text: Todo va muy bien hoy.
examples.trans: Everything is going very well today.

examples.text: El té sale bien caliente.
examples.trans: The tea comes out nice and hot.

meanings.note: Built from boca (mouth).

examples.text: El bocado está aquí.
examples.trans: The bite is here.

examples.text: Vemos los bocados desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the bites from the door.

cambiar.gloss: to change; to swap; to exchange

meanings.en: to change; to swap; to exchange
meanings.note: Cambiar de habitación/camisa uses de before the noun.

examples.text: Cambio las toallas cada mañana.
examples.trans: I change the towels every morning.

examples.text: Cambiamos la mesa de sitio.
examples.trans: We moved the table to a new spot.

meanings.note: Core feminine noun for the human or animal face; central to Spanish idioms like 'dar la cara' ('to step up / take responsibility') and 'verle la cara a alguien'.
Colloquially, 'tener cara' or 'qué cara' means to be shameless or brazen. Also feminine singular of the adjective caro ('expensive').

examples.text: Pero le ves la cara, te emociona, te llega.
examples.trans: But you see her face, she moves you, she gets right to you.

examples.text: ¡Qué cara más dura tienes presentándote aquí sin avisar!
examples.trans: What nerve you have showing up here unannounced!

meanings.note: Woodworker (feminine: la carpintera).

examples.text: El carpintero está aquí.
examples.trans: The carpenter is here.

examples.text: Vemos los carpinteros desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the carpenters from the door.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb; polite negative imperative: no celebre.

examples.text: Esta noche celebramos la apertura del nuevo café con amigos.
examples.trans: Tonight we are celebrating the opening of the new café with friends.

examples.text: Toda la familia celebra el cumpleaños de la abuela en el jardín.
examples.trans: The whole family celebrates Grandmother's birthday in the garden.

meanings.note: Cola de carpintero / cola blanca is wood glue; hacer cola means 'to queue'.

examples.text: Mateo usa cola seca para fijar el fieltro.
examples.trans: Mateo uses dry glue to secure the felt.

examples.text: Deja secar la cola de madera toda la noche.
examples.trans: Let the wood glue dry all night.

meanings.note: Regular -er verb.

examples.text: Comemos juntos a las dos de la tarde.
examples.trans: We have lunch together at two in the afternoon.

examples.text: Comí un trozo de bizcocho de limón.
examples.trans: I ate a piece of lemon sponge cake.

meanings.note: Combines with mí/ti to form conmigo ('with me') and contigo ('with you').

examples.text: Tomo café con leche caliente.
examples.trans: I take coffee with hot milk.

examples.text: Habla con calma, por favor.
examples.trans: Speak calmly, please.

meanings.note: Bound paper notebook.

examples.text: El cuaderno está aquí.
examples.trans: The notebook is here.

examples.text: Vemos los cuadernos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the notebooks from the door.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.text: Tenemos cuatro mesas dentro.
examples.trans: We have four tables inside.

examples.text: La habitación cuatro da al patio.
examples.trans: Room four looks out onto the courtyard.

meanings.note: Interrogative adverb with written accent.

examples.text: ¿Cómo se llama usted?
examples.trans: What is your name?

examples.text: ¿Cómo encuentro la ferretería?
examples.trans: How do I find the hardware shop?

meanings.note: Links possession, origin, material (de madera), and contents (taza de té).

examples.text: Es una mesa redonda de madera.
examples.trans: It is a round wooden table.

examples.text: Vengo de la estación de tren.
examples.trans: I am coming from the train station.

meanings.note: With a noun object (le debo la verdad), means 'to owe'; before an infinitive, means 'should / ought to'.

examples.text: Le debo diez euros de cambio.
examples.trans: I owe you ten euros in change.

examples.text: Todo funciona como debe ser.
examples.trans: Everything works as it should.

meanings.note: Querer decir means 'to mean'.

examples.text: ¿Qué dice la carta exactamente?
examples.trans: What does the letter say exactly?

examples.text: Dime la verdad sin miedo.
examples.trans: Tell me the truth without fear.

meanings.note: Dejar de + infinitive means 'to stop doing something'.

examples.text: Dejo las llaves en el mostrador.
examples.trans: I leave the keys on the counter.

examples.text: Déjame ayudarte con esa caja.
examples.trans: Let me help you with that box.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition de + masculine article el.

examples.text: El bizcocho acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The cake just came out of the oven.

examples.text: Soy vecino del barrio.
examples.trans: I am a neighbour from the quarter.

meanings.note: Diez sobre diez = ten out of ten.

examples.text: Faltan diez minutos para empezar.
examples.trans: There are ten minutes left before starting.

examples.text: Su recepción merece un diez.
examples.trans: Your front desk deserves a ten.

meanings.note: Definite article; also appears before feminine nouns starting with stressed /a/ (el agua, el asa).

examples.text: El patio tiene mucha luz.
examples.trans: The courtyard has plenty of light.

examples.text: Pásame el libro de reservas.
examples.trans: Pass me the reservation book.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> ie: empiezo); empezar a + infinitive.

examples.text: Empiezo el turno a las siete.
examples.trans: I start my shift at seven.

examples.text: La película empezó cinco minutos tarde.
examples.trans: The film started five minutes late.

meanings.note: Expresses location inside or on top of a surface (en la mesa = on the table).

examples.text: Las tazas están en la mesa.
examples.trans: The cups are on the table.

examples.text: Vivimos en Valencia todo el año.
examples.trans: We live in Valencia all year.

meanings.note: Sigue entera = it is still in one piece.

examples.text: Es una pieza entera.
examples.trans: It is a whole piece.

examples.text: ¿Y su taza dentro? ¿Sigue entera?
examples.trans: And your cup inside? Is it still in one piece?

entrar.gloss: to come in; to go in; to enter

meanings.en: to come in; to go in; to enter
meanings.note: Pairs with en in Spain (entrar en la posada).

examples.text: Entra mucha luz por el balcón.
examples.trans: Plenty of light comes in through the balcony.

examples.text: Entramos en la tienda para resguardarnos.
examples.trans: We stepped into the shop to shelter.

meanings.note: Regular -ir verb with irregular past participle escrito.

examples.text: Escribo la nota con lápiz azul.
examples.trans: I write the note in blue pencil.

examples.text: Mi hermano me escribió una postal corta.
examples.trans: My brother wrote me a short postcard.

meanings.note: Neuter pronoun; por eso = that is why.

examples.text: Por eso traje dos paraguas.
examples.trans: That is why I brought two umbrellas.

examples.text: ¿Qué significa eso exactamente?
examples.trans: What does that mean exactly?

esperar.gloss: to wait; to wait for; to hope

meanings.en: to wait; to wait for; to hope
meanings.note: Covers both 'wait (for)' and 'hope'.

examples.text: Espere un momento, por favor.
examples.trans: Wait a moment, please.

examples.text: Esperamos que descanse muy bien.
examples.trans: We hope you rest very well.

esquina.gloss: corner (outer street corner or cake corner)

meanings.en: corner (outer street corner or cake corner)
meanings.note: Outer corner where two streets meet, or the crisp corner of a baking tray.

examples.text: La esquina está aquí.
examples.trans: The corner is here.

examples.text: Vemos las esquinas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the corners from the door.

meanings.note: Pairs with locations (está en el patio) and temporary states (está caliente).

examples.text: El desayuno ya está listo.
examples.trans: Breakfast is ready now.

examples.text: ¿Dónde están las llaves de latón?
examples.trans: Where are the brass keys?

meanings.note: Regular 4-form adjective.

examples.text: Rocío es muy estricta con los tiempos del horno.
examples.trans: Rocio is very strict about oven timings.

examples.text: Seguimos normas estrictas de limpieza en la cocina.
examples.trans: We follow strict cleanliness rules in the kitchen.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('el fondo'). Used in photography/video for a backdrop ('un fondo blanco'), in audio/staging for 'in the background' ('de fondo'), and figuratively in 'en el fondo' ('deep down').

examples.text: Yo pondría un fondo blanco ahí. Tengo esta pared libre.
examples.trans: I would put a white backdrop there. I have this wall free.

examples.text: En el fondo es una buena persona, aunque tenga mucho carácter.
examples.trans: Deep down she is a good person, even if she has a strong temper.

frente.gloss: forehead; front (frente a = in front of)

meanings.en: forehead; front (frente a = in front of)
meanings.note: La frente (f) = forehead; frente a frente = face to face.

examples.text: La frente está aquí.
examples.trans: The forehead is here.

examples.text: Vemos las frentes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the foreheads from the door.

meanings.note: Plural-only feminine noun in Spain: las gafas.

examples.text: ¿Dónde he dejado mis gafas?
examples.trans: Where did I leave my glasses?

examples.text: Lleva unas gafas redondas.
examples.trans: He wears round glasses.

grande.gloss: big; large; great (gran before sg noun)

meanings.en: big; large; great (gran before sg noun)
meanings.note: Shortens to gran before any singular noun (un gran libro, una gran idea).

examples.text: Tenemos una mesa grande en el patio.
examples.trans: We have a big table in the courtyard.

examples.text: Es una gran noticia para todos.
examples.trans: It is great news for everyone.

meanings.note: Impersonal present form hay means 'there is / there are'; haber que + infinitive = must / need to.

examples.text: Hay pan caliente en la cocina.
examples.trans: There is warm bread in the kitchen.

examples.text: Ya hemos preparado las habitaciones.
examples.trans: We have already prepared the rooms.

hacer.gloss: to do; to make; ago (hace + time)

meanings.en: to do; to make; ago (hace + time)
meanings.note: Irregular: hago, hice, hecho; hace tres años = three years ago.

examples.text: La panadera hace pan fresco cada mañana.
examples.trans: The baker bakes fresh bread every morning.

examples.text: Llegó hace diez minutos.
examples.trans: She arrived ten minutes ago.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! = See you later!; ¡Hasta mañana! = See you tomorrow!

examples.text: Sigue recto hasta el puente.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead as far as the bridge.

examples.text: Nos quedamos hasta el viernes.
examples.trans: We are staying until Friday.

meanings.note: Plural los hombres.

examples.text: El hombre está aquí.
examples.trans: The man is here.

examples.text: Vemos los hombres desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the men from the door.

meanings.note: Built from horno (oven).

examples.text: La panadera hornea bizcochos cada viernes.
examples.trans: The baker bakes sponge cakes every Friday.

examples.text: Esta mañana horneamos pan crujiente.
examples.trans: This morning we baked crusty bread.

meanings.note: Ir a + infinitive expresses near future ('going to do').

examples.text: Voy a abrir la puerta ahora.
examples.trans: I am going to open the door now.

examples.text: ¿Cómo va todo esta mañana?
examples.trans: How is everything going this morning?

meanings.note: Plural changes -z to -ces (los jueces); common gender el/la juez (or feminine la jueza).

examples.text: Mateo sirvió hoy como nuestro juez principal en la prueba de tartas.
examples.trans: Mateo served today as our chief judge in the cake tasting.

examples.text: Los tres jueces aplaudieron cuando probaron el último plato.
examples.trans: All three judges applauded when they tasted the final dish.

meanings.note: Definite feminine singular article before nouns; direct-object feminine pronoun before/attached to verbs.

examples.text: La puerta del patio es azul.
examples.trans: The courtyard door is blue.

examples.text: La habitación tiene mucha luz.
examples.trans: The room has plenty of light.

meanings.note: Al lado = on the side / next door.

examples.text: El lado está aquí.
examples.trans: The side is here.

examples.text: Vemos los lados desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the sides from the door.

meanings.note: Yellow copper-zinc alloy used for keys, lamps, and valves.

examples.text: El latón es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The brass is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el latón.
examples.trans: We talk about the brass.

meanings.note: Tu letra means 'your handwriting'.

examples.text: La letra está aquí.
examples.trans: The handwriting is here.

examples.text: Vemos las letras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the handwritings from the door.

limpiar.gloss: to clean; to polish; to wipe

meanings.en: to clean; to polish; to wipe
meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Limpio el mostrador con un paño seco.
examples.trans: I wipe the counter with a dry cloth.

examples.text: Limpiamos los farolillos para la fiesta.
examples.trans: We polished the lanterns for the party.

lo.gloss: it / him (direct object); the (neuter before adj/que)

meanings.en: it / him (direct object); the (neuter before adj/que)
meanings.note: Direct object pronoun before verbs (lo veo), and neuter article in lo que ('what') or lo mejor ('the best').

examples.text: Ya lo veo encima del estante.
examples.trans: I see it now on the shelf.

examples.text: Lo mejor del patio es la calma.
examples.trans: The best part of the courtyard is the calm.

meanings.note: Plural los lápices; a lápiz = in pencil.

examples.text: El lápiz está aquí.
examples.trans: The pencil is here.

examples.text: Vemos los lápices desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the pencils from the door.

meanings.note: Standard workshop tool for driving nails or tapping metal.

examples.text: El tenedor entra suave en la tarta tres sin necesitar un martillo.
examples.trans: The fork glides smoothly into cake three without needing a hammer.

examples.text: Mateo guardó el martillo y los clavos en su caja de herramientas.
examples.trans: Mateo put the hammer and nails away in his toolbox.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb with a c -> qu spelling change before -e (mastiqué, mastique).

examples.text: Dejad que nuestro juez mastique tranquilo antes de pedirle la nota.
examples.trans: Let our judge chew in peace before asking him for the score.

examples.text: El azúcar tostado del molde dos hacía mucho ruido al masticar.
examples.trans: The toasted sugar on Tin Two made a lot of noise when chewing.

meanings.note: Used for gold, silver, or bronze prize medals (medalla de oro).

examples.text: ¡Un diez sobre diez de Mateo vale más que tres medallas de oro!
examples.trans: A ten out of ten from Mateo is worth more than three gold medals!

examples.text: La pastelera ganó una medalla en el concurso de dulces de Valencia.
examples.trans: The pastry chef won a medal at the Valencia sweets competition.

meanings.note: Media vuelta = half-turn (turn around); medio vaso = half a glass.

examples.text: Es una pieza media.
examples.trans: It is a half piece.

examples.text: Oh, qué amable es usted, señor. Solo medio vaso.
examples.trans: Oh, how kind you are, sir. Just half a glass.

meanings.note: Irregular 1st sg merezco.

examples.text: Este café merece cinco estrellas.
examples.trans: This coffee deserves five stars.

examples.text: Después de correr, mereces un descanso.
examples.trans: After running, you deserve a rest.

meanings.note: Dining, cafe, or courtyard table.

examples.text: La mesa está aquí.
examples.trans: The table is here.

examples.text: Vemos las mesas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the tables from the door.

meanings.note: Plural mis (mi llave / mis llaves); unaccented, distinct from pronoun mí.

examples.text: Mi maleta es azul marino.
examples.trans: My suitcase is navy blue.

examples.text: Mis apuntes están en el bolsillo.
examples.trans: My notes are in my pocket.

mirar.gloss: to look; to look at; to watch

meanings.en: to look; to look at; to watch
meanings.note: Needs no preposition for 'at' (mira el reloj = look at the clock).

examples.text: Mira qué sol hace esta mañana.
examples.trans: Look how sunny it is this morning.

examples.text: Miramos el mapa antes de salir.
examples.trans: We look at the map before going out.

nada.gloss: nothing; not at all (de nada = you're welcome)

meanings.en: nothing; not at all (de nada = you're welcome)
meanings.note: No pasa nada = no problem; nada de... = no ... at all.

examples.text: Tranquilo, no pasa nada.
examples.trans: Easy now, there is no problem at all.

examples.text: No queda nada de mantequilla.
examples.trans: There is no butter left at all.

meanings.note: Requires no before the verb when nadie follows (no hay nadie).

examples.text: Todavía no hay nadie en el patio.
examples.trans: There is nobody in the courtyard yet.

examples.text: Nadie conoce mejor este edificio.
examples.trans: Nobody knows this building better.

meanings.note: Ni... ni... = neither... nor...; ni una gota = not a single drop.

examples.text: No cae ni una sola gota.
examples.trans: Not a single drop is falling.

examples.text: No tengo ni papel ni bolígrafo.
examples.trans: I have neither paper nor pen.

meanings.note: Placed directly before the verb (or object pronouns) to negate a sentence.

examples.text: Hoy no llueve en Valencia.
examples.trans: Today it is not raining in Valencia.

examples.text: No se preocupe por la hora.
examples.trans: Do not worry about the time.

nos.gloss: us; to us; each other (¡Nos vemos!)

meanings.en: us; to us; each other (¡Nos vemos!)
meanings.note: First-person plural object/reflexive/reciprocal pronoun.

examples.text: ¡Nos vemos mañana por la mañana!
examples.trans: See you tomorrow morning!

examples.text: Nos alegra mucho la noticia.
examples.trans: The news makes us very glad.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender and number with the thing possessed (nuestro patio, nuestra posada).

examples.text: Nuestra posada tiene ocho habitaciones.
examples.trans: Our guesthouse has eight rooms.

examples.text: Nuestros vecinos toman café aquí.
examples.trans: Our neighbours have coffee here.

meanings.en: gold (precious metal, color, or something of great value)
meanings.note: Masculine noun. Frequently used figuratively in the idiom 'valer oro' ('to be worth its weight in gold / to be priceless'), as when Paquita savors the fresh country air of her hometown.

meanings.en: oros (suit of golden coins in the Spanish card deck)
meanings.note: In the plural ('los oros'), refers to the suit of coins in the traditional Spanish deck of cards ('la baraja española').

examples.text: Este aire... (ASPIRA) Este aire vale oro.
examples.trans: This air... (INHALES) This air is worth its weight in gold.

examples.text: Esa representante tiene un corazón de oro aunque a veces pierda los nervios.
examples.trans: That talent agent has a heart of gold even though she loses her temper sometimes.

meanings.note: Spanish never puts un/una before otro (otra taza = another cup; otra vez = again).

examples.text: ¿Quiere otra taza de café?
examples.trans: Would you like another cup of coffee?

examples.text: Míralo otra vez a la luz.
examples.trans: Look at it again in the light.

meanings.note: Ni una palabra = not a word.

examples.text: La palabra está aquí.
examples.trans: The word is here.

examples.text: Vemos las palabras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the words from the door.

meanings.note: Plural los papeles.

examples.text: El papel está aquí.
examples.trans: The paper is here.

examples.text: Vemos los papeles desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the papers from the door.

meanings.note: Marks destination, recipient (para ti), deadline, and minutes to the hour (cinco para las doce).

examples.text: Este paquete blanco es para mi hermano.
examples.trans: This white parcel is for my brother.

examples.text: Faltan diez minutos para las doce.
examples.trans: It is ten minutes to twelve.

pasar.gloss: to pass; to come in (¡Pase!); to happen

meanings.en: to pass; to come in (¡Pase!); to happen
meanings.note: ¿Qué pasa? = What's wrong?; No pasa nada = No problem.

examples.text: ¡Pase, por favor, y siéntese!
examples.trans: Come in, please, and have a seat!

examples.text: Pasa la farmacia verde a la derecha.
examples.trans: Pass the green pharmacy on your right.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> i: pido, pidió).

examples.text: Pido un café con leche, por favor.
examples.trans: I will order a coffee with milk, please.

examples.text: El cartero me pidió una firma.
examples.trans: The postman asked me for a signature.

meanings.note: Hermano pequeño = younger brother; de pequeño = as a child.

examples.text: Es una pieza pequeña.
examples.trans: It is a small piece.

examples.text: Hay una pequeña tarjeta de cartón atada al asa.
examples.trans: There is a small cardboard card tied to the handle.

examples.text: A ti ya te pillaré, Canelón. Vámonos.
examples.trans: I'll catch up with you later, Canelón. Let's go.

examples.text: Yo pillar
examples.trans: I pillar

poner.gloss: to put; to set; to become (ponerse + adj)

meanings.en: to put; to set; to become (ponerse + adj)
meanings.note: Irregular: pongo, pon, puse, puesto; ponerse nervioso = get nervous.

examples.text: Pongo dos tazas limpias en la mesa.
examples.trans: I put two clean cups on the table.

examples.text: Pon la maleta junto al mostrador.
examples.trans: Set the suitcase beside the counter.

por.gloss: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)

meanings.en: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)
meanings.note: Por la mañana = in the morning; por favor = please; gracias por = thanks for.

examples.text: Paseamos por el casco antiguo.
examples.trans: We stroll through the old quarter.

examples.text: Por la mañana entra mucho sol.
examples.trans: In the morning plenty of sun comes in.

meanings.note: Shortens to primer before masculine singular nouns (el primer día); also used as adverb ('first').

examples.text: Hoy es mi primer día de trabajo.
examples.trans: Today is my first day of work.

examples.text: La primera habitación está libre.
examples.trans: The first room is vacant.

probar.gloss: to try; to taste; to test

meanings.en: to try; to taste; to test
meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: pruebo).

examples.text: Prueba este pan con aceite de oliva.
examples.trans: Try this bread with olive oil.

examples.text: Ayer probamos la mermelada de manzana.
examples.trans: Yesterday we tasted the apple jam.

meanings.note: Covers room doors, street doors, and courtyard gates.

examples.text: La puerta está aquí.
examples.trans: The door is here.

examples.text: Vemos las puertas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the doors from the door.

meanings.note: Core connector and relative pronoun (unaccented, distinct from interrogative qué).

examples.text: Espero que descanses muy bien.
examples.trans: I hope that you rest very well.

examples.text: El pan de esta panadería huele genial.
examples.trans: The bread that The baker bakes smells great.

meanings.note: Sin querer = by accident; querer decir = to mean.

examples.text: ¿Quiere usted café o té caliente?
examples.trans: Would you like coffee or hot tea?

examples.text: Lo abrí sin querer.
examples.trans: I opened it by accident.

seguir.gloss: to continue; to keep (doing); to go straight (seguir recto)

meanings.en: to continue; to keep (doing); to go straight (seguir recto)
meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> i: sigo, sigue, siguió); seguir + gerund = keep doing.

examples.text: Sigue todo recto hasta el puente.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead to the bridge.

examples.text: ¿El agua sigue caliente?
examples.trans: Is the water still hot?

meanings.note: Also a masculine noun (un segundo = one second).

examples.text: Es una pieza segunda.
examples.trans: It is a second piece.

examples.text: Segunda: Te he echado de menos estos tres años.
examples.trans: Second: I missed you these three years.

meanings.note: Con seguridad = safely / for sure.

examples.text: La seguridad está aquí.
examples.trans: The safety is here.

examples.text: Vemos las seguridades desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the safetys from the door.

meanings.note: Takes el when talking about someone (el señor Martín), no article when addressing directly (¡Buenos días, señor!).

examples.text: El señor está aquí.
examples.trans: The sir is here.

examples.text: Vemos los señores desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the sirs from the door.

meanings.note: Followed by bare nouns (sin azúcar, sin sal) or infinitives (sin abrir = unopened).

examples.text: Tomo el té sin azúcar, gracias.
examples.trans: I take my tea without sugar, thank you.

examples.text: Salió de casa sin abrigo.
examples.trans: He left home without a coat.

sobre.gloss: on; upon; about; out of (nueve sobre diez)

meanings.en: on; upon; about; out of (nueve sobre diez)
meanings.note: Sobre todo = above all / mostly; also a homograph noun el sobre ('envelope').

examples.text: Deja la llave sobre el mostrador.
examples.trans: Leave the key on the counter.

examples.text: Sacó nueve sobre diez en la prueba.
examples.trans: She scored nine out of ten on the test.

solo.gloss: only; just (also adj solo/sola = alone / single)

meanings.en: only; just (also adj solo/sola = alone / single)
meanings.note: Unaccented in modern RAE spelling; café solo = black espresso.

examples.text: Solo necesito cinco minutos más.
examples.trans: I only need five more minutes.

examples.text: Queda una sola habitación libre.
examples.trans: Only a single room remains vacant.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine.

examples.text: Es una pieza suave.
examples.trans: It is a soft piece.

examples.text: Y mire: esta chaqueta de lana suave está limpia y nueva. Pruébela.
examples.trans: And look: this soft wool cardigan is clean and unworn. Try it on.

meanings.note: El sábado means 'on Saturday'; los sábados means 'on Saturdays'.

examples.text: Los sábados vamos temprano al mercado de la plaza.
examples.trans: On Saturdays we go early to the market in the square.

examples.text: Este sábado abrimos las ventanas de la galería.
examples.trans: This Saturday we open the sunroom windows.

meanings.note: Accented sí means 'yes' (distinct from unaccented si = 'if').

examples.text: Sí, la habitación está lista.
examples.trans: Yes, the room is ready.

examples.text: ¡Claro que sí, pase usted!
examples.trans: Of course, come right in!

meanings.note: Plural los talleres.

examples.text: El taller está aquí.
examples.trans: The workshop is here.

examples.text: Vemos los talleres desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the workshops from the door.

meanings.note: Usual word in Spain for a sweet tart or birthday cake.

examples.text: Hay tarta de chocolate para el postre.
examples.trans: There is chocolate cake for dessert.

examples.text: Mi abuela hace una tarta de manzana riquísima.
examples.trans: My grandmother makes a delicious apple tart.

meanings.note: Object/reflexive pronoun corresponding to tú.

examples.text: Te guardo un rollo de canela.
examples.trans: I am saving a cinnamon roll for you.

examples.text: ¿Cómo te llamas?
examples.trans: What is your name?

meanings.note: Standard word for an eating fork (tenedor de postre = dessert fork).

examples.text: Mateo se llevó un tenedor lleno de tarta tibia a la boca.
examples.trans: Mateo put a forkful of warm cake into his mouth.

examples.text: Coloca el tenedor a la izquierda del plato y el cuchillo a la derecha.
examples.trans: Place the fork to the left of the plate and the knife to the right.

meanings.note: Built from té (tea).

examples.text: La tetera está aquí.
examples.trans: The teapot is here.

examples.text: Vemos las teteras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the teapots from the door.

meanings.note: Todo el día = the whole day; todo el mundo = everyone; sobre todo = mostly.

examples.text: Todo está limpio y en su sitio.
examples.trans: Everything is clean and in its place.

examples.text: Camina todo recto por esta calle.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead down this street.

meanings.note: ¡Toma! = Here you go!; tomar un café = have a coffee.

examples.text: ¿Qué quiere tomar para desayunar?
examples.trans: What would you like to have for breakfast?

examples.text: Toma, aquí tienes la linterna.
examples.trans: Here you go, here is the flashlight.

meanings.note: Said alone to reassure someone ('Easy, don't worry!').

examples.text: Es una pieza tranquila.
examples.trans: It is a quiet piece.

examples.text: Seca, calentita y tranquila. Ahora decidme qué falta.
examples.trans: Dry, warm, and quiet. Now tell me what is missing.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.text: Ponemos tres mesas bajo el árbol.
examples.trans: We set three tables under the tree.

examples.text: Empieza con tres frases cortas.
examples.trans: Start with three short sentences.

trocito.gloss: tiny piece; small slice; little bit

meanings.en: tiny piece; small slice; little bit
meanings.note: Diminutive (-ito) of trozo ('piece, slice').

examples.text: Cada trocito de papel roto coincide como las mitades de una taza.
examples.trans: Every tiny bit of torn paper lines up like the halves of a teacup.

examples.text: Mateo pidió otro trocito pequeño de la esquina de la tarta.
examples.trans: Mateo asked for another small corner slice of the cake.

meanings.note: Un trozo de bizcocho = a piece of cake.

examples.text: El trozo está aquí.
examples.trans: The piece is here.

examples.text: Vemos los trozos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the pieces from the door.

meanings.note: Describes specialized skill or precision; as a feminine noun, la técnica means 'technique'.

examples.text: Solo por seguridad técnica, Mateo quiso probar otro trocito de tarta.
examples.trans: Purely for technical safety, Mateo wanted to test another small slice of cake.

examples.text: El libro explica todos los detalles técnicos de los relojes antiguos.
examples.trans: The book explains all the technical details of antique clocks.

meanings.note: Forms: un (m sg), una (f sg), unos (m pl 'some/about'), unas (f pl).

examples.text: Quiero un café caliente, por favor.
examples.trans: I would like a hot coffee, please.

examples.text: Hay una mesa libre en el patio.
examples.trans: There is a free table in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Spain's ubiquitous single-word confirmation (from valer).

examples.text: —Nos vemos a las doce. —¡Vale!
examples.trans: 'See you at twelve.' 'Okay!'

examples.text: Vale, yo llevo las tazas al patio.
examples.trans: Alright, I will carry the cups to the courtyard.

meanings.note: Irregular: veo, vi, visto.

examples.text: Desde aquí veo el puente de piedra.
examples.trans: From here I see the stone bridge.

examples.text: ¡Nos vemos luego en el patio!
examples.trans: See you later in the courtyard!

meanings.note: La verdad = honestly / the truth.

examples.text: La verdad está aquí.
examples.trans: The truth is here.

examples.text: Vemos las verdades desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the truths from the door.

meanings.note: Changes to e before words starting with /i/ sound (i- or hi-).

examples.text: Servimos café caliente y pan fresco.
examples.trans: We serve hot coffee and fresh bread.

examples.text: Son las siete y cuarto.
examples.trans: It is quarter past seven.
